title: Type Confusion & Language Specifics
description: Runtime coercion and language-specific input handling mistakes.

attacks.name: JS == coercion
attacks.desc: JavaScript loose equality can make unlike values compare equal when an application expects exact identity.
attacks.prevention: Use strict equality and explicit type conversion for security decisions instead of JavaScript loose equality.

attacks.name: Array vs string
attacks.desc: Frameworks may parse repeated or bracketed parameters as arrays where application code expects a string.
attacks.prevention: Reject unexpected arrays or objects at request boundaries when an endpoint expects one scalar value.

attacks.name: Object injection
attacks.desc: Nested parameter syntax can inject object properties into a deserialized structure if input is not constrained.
attacks.prevention: Allowlist object keys and block prototype-related names before merging untrusted nested parameters.

attacks.name: PHP magic hash
attacks.desc: PHP loose comparisons can treat distinct hashes beginning with numeric-looking 0e strings as equal.
attacks.prevention: Use strict comparisons for hashes and authentication values; never compare password hashes with PHP loose equality.

attacks.name: PHP loose compare
attacks.desc: PHP functions and loose comparisons can produce surprising results for arrays, strings, and numeric values.

attacks.name: Python bool is int
attacks.desc: In Python, booleans are integer subclasses, so True can collide with numeric identifiers in careless comparisons.

attacks.name: Ruby nil/false truthiness
attacks.desc: Treating Ruby nil and false as interchangeable can confuse absent values with explicit negative decisions.

attacks.name: Integer overflow
attacks.desc: A value beyond an integer type's range can wrap or fail and alter quantity, balance, or index calculations.

attacks.name: Float precision
attacks.desc: Binary floating-point rounding can make money comparisons or totals differ from decimal expectations.

attacks.name: Format string
attacks.desc: Untrusted format strings can change output or memory behavior in affected formatting APIs.

attacks.name: Regex injection
attacks.desc: A user-supplied regular expression can change matching logic or consume excessive CPU.

attacks.name: Expression evaluation
attacks.desc: Passing user input to an expression evaluator can turn a filter value into executable logic.
